text:
rachel: deploy-bot just held the promo for v2026-03-21 due to artifact checksum mismatch during preflight. blocking cut until we decide.

deploy-bot: [automated] Promotion blocked: artifact-checksum-mismatch for registry.prod/release/v2026-03-21. preflight job `preflight-integrations-3` failed (artifact pulled differs from manifest). logs: https://ci.redwood/integration/1812345670/logs

dan: that sounds like a multipart reupload race where composer finished with different ordered chunks. we saw this pattern in staging once. can we compare storage object generations?

sre-oncall: pulled object generations. origin has gen:145 and gen:146; gen:146 size differs and digest != manifest entry. I can quarantine gen:146 and re-add a retention tag to gen:145 to avoid GC.

evan: if gen:145 is the last-good, we should pin the manifest to that digest and re-run preflight. pin+verify is least risky during change window. fallback plan: if preflight still fails, revert to tag stable-2026-03-20 and run rollback playbook.

release-manager: agree. we need clear steps and owners. decision options:
- A: pin to last-good digest (sha256:77aabbcc), re-run preflight, manual canary after verification.
- B: attempt regional invalidation and recompose gen:146 (noisy).
- C: abort promo and rollback to stable tag.

dan: my vote A. pin and verify. I can run the promote once SRE confirms gen:145 is available in all regions.

sre-oncall: confirmation: gen:145 available in us-west1 and eu-west1, ap-south needs a replicate (ETA 9m). quaratined gen:146 -> quarantined_by:sre-oncall. also added retention:artifact-preserve until 2026-03-23.

deploy-bot: [automated] Manual promotion queued: promote --repo prod --manifest-digest sha256:77aabbcc --requester dan

dan: running promote now (dry-run then apply).
```bash
# dry-run
deployctl promote --repo prod --manifest-digest sha256:77aabbcc --dry-run
# apply
deployctl promote --repo prod --manifest-digest sha256:77aabbcc --reason "pin last-good after multipart checksum flip"
```

evan: I'll create monitoring checks to watch canary errors and token-level anomaly dashboards. also drafting release-note line: "Rollout delayed briefly for artifact verification; pinned to last-known-good artifact and verifying regional replication."

release-manager: who will rerun preflight? dan?

dan: I'll kick preflight rerun and constrain to us-west1 runners to avoid edge cache skew. bumped timeout to 50m.

deploy-bot: [automated] preflight-integrations-3 rerun started by dan. logs: https://ci.redwood/integration/1812345670/rerun

sre-oncall: replication to ap-south completed. verified checksums from three regions match sha256:77aabbcc. quarantined gen:146 remains isolated.

evan: preflight passed health checks at 2026-03-21T18:05Z. we should still keep canary disabled and enable manually after a short verification window.

release-manager: decision recorded: pin to sha256:77aabbcc, quarantine suspect gen:146, re-run preflight (passed), manual canary enable at 18:20Z, monitor 30m, then full rollout if stable. create follow-up ticket for artifact-upload team to add atomic manifest commit and stronger end-to-end checks.

dan: noting rollback trigger: if canary error rate > 1% or registry 5xx spikes > 0.5% in the 30m window, execute rollback to stable-2026-03-20 and notify customers.

sre-oncall: applied tags to prevent GC and scheduled post-release cleanup task for quarantined gen:146 after postmortem.

deploy-bot: [automated] Promotion ready for manual proceed. state: pinned=sha256:77aabbcc, quarantined=gen:146, preflight=passed.

release-manager: thanks all. publishing short release note and opening postmortem ticket. keeping thread open until canary window complete. :white_check_mark:
